messages:
acm-support: FYI customer reported sudden p99 spike for EU users. Latency jumped from ~120ms -> ~1.2s in the last hour. They say requests appear to be routed to us-east-1. Trace id: trc_0a9f7c. Attached full HAR and their sample request.
observability: Got the trace id — here's the top-level span path we see:
```
> client -> eu-central-1 (ingest) -> us-east-1 (model-v2) -> us-west-2 (kv-cache) -> eu-central-1 (response)
```
span timings: ingest 30ms, us-east exec 820ms, kv-cache roundtrip 280ms.
netops: Wait, kv-cache in us-west-2? That would explain the extra hop. Any chance of a mis-tagged cache region or a stale peering entry?
eng-runtime: Looking. Smart routing fallback shows model v2.0 unavailable in eu-central-1 for that customer (quota/placement), so routing policy fell back to the nearest compatible variant — it picked us-east-1. That shouldn't trigger a cache call to us-west-2 though.
acm-support: Customer repro steps they sent:
```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.dev
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
Content-Type: application/json
{"model":"redwood-model-v2","input":"hello"}
```
They included SDK region param set to null (default).
observability: Expanded trace shows a KV rehydrate request originated from the us-east-1 serving node to a fallback cache shard in us-west-2. Rehydrate log: `cache-miss -> shard-27@us-west-2`. Looks like shard assignment changed during a rolling reshard.
infra-oncall: If shard mapping moved, some serving nodes may still reference old shard endpoints. Did we push a reshard that didn't update the routing table? Check /internal/cache/shard-map last update.
eng-runtime: I can repro locally by forcing model-unavailable in eu. Commands:
```
# simulate request force-fallback
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Request-ID: repro-101" -d '{"model":"redwood-model-v2","input":"test"}' https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -w "\n%{time_total}s\n"
```
Without region override I see time_total ~1.05s, with `-H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-central-1"` it stays stuck because fallback overrides region. If you set `X-Force-Region: eu-central-1` (workaround) the request fails fast with 409 model-unavailable (preferred to silent cross-continent fallback).
netops: OK looks like root cause: reshard pushed a new mapping but some cache proxies (us-east-1) still using previous mapping and routed rehydrate to us-west-2. That created cross-continent RTT.
acm-support: Customer impact: elevated latency and extra egress costs. They asked if there's a quick workaround on their side.
eng-runtime: Workaround options: 1) SDK/HTTP header `X-Force-Region` to avoid silent cross-continent fallback (will return explicit 4xx). 2) In Console set project routing policy to "prefer-local-only" so it won't pick cross-continent fallbacks. We'll document both.
observability: Evidence attached (span dump + reshard logs): `reshard: map_v15 -> map_v16 at 2026-03-17T10:12Z, partial rollout to eu proxies still pending`.
infra-oncall: Immediate fix: roll back shard-map to map_v15 for a short window and trigger a coordinated resync to proxies. I'll schedule that now and post updates here.
eng-runtime: Longer fix: add consistency barrier to resharding flow so serving nodes re-resolve shard-map before doing remote cache rehydrates. I'll open a ticket and prioritize.
acm-support: Noted. I'll tell the customer the workaround and ETA. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
pagerduty-bot: Incident linked PD-4882, severity: low-med, assigned to infra-oncall.
netops: I'll keep monitoring traces for any other cross-continent kv hits and post alerts if spike repeats.
acm-support: Closing loop with customer now — will ping once we roll back.
